newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan money growth seen unchanged in Jan.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan money growth seen unchanged in Jan.

text.p: Year-on-year growth in Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs), the key gauge of money supply, is expected to be around 3.2 percent in January, unchanged from December, economists said on Friday.
Economists polled by Reuters in Tokyo gave estimates for growth in money supply ranging from 3.1 percent to 3.3 percent in January.
In December, money supply grew a preliminary 3.2 percent from a year earlier.
The January figure will be released by the Bank of Japan at 8.50 a.m. on Tuesday (2350 GMT Monday).
Japan"s money supply growth has edged down since mid-1996, reflecting sluggish economic recovery.

"An increase in money flow from private sector to public sector by about one trillion yen from a year earlier could help lower money supply growth slightly in January," said Atsushi Takeda, an economist at DKB Research Institute.
Economists said a lack of growth in bank lending continued to keep money supply growth at a low level.

The average balance of bank lending by Japan's 149 banks dipped 0.2 percent in January from a year ago to 534.36 trillion yen, the fourth month in a row of year-on-year declines, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Friday.
